name: Erasmus Deffebach
role: Superintendent of the Medora Stage and Forwarding Co.; later cattle foreman
bio: Erasmus 'Rassie' Deffebach came to Medora from Spearfish in the Black Hills in spring 1884, renting the company stable that June and moving his family to town in August. As superintendent of the Medora Stage and Forwarding Co., he bought horses at Helena in September 1884 and announced that coaches to Deadwood would start on October 6, and he signed a certificate with Arthur T. Packard that month. In early 1885 the paper reported news of a family fortune awaiting the Deffebach heirs in Germany, and he and J. C. Fisher ran Medora's roller rink. In July 1885 M. Wadsworth hired him as foreman for the Bad Lands Cattle Co., and he moved his family to Dickinson; in January 1886 he went to the E6 camp.
